purpose: Prove that separate AI sessions can repair bounded RCL-owned Android transaction, reactive binding and lifecycle semantics without seeing canonical inputs or oracle edits.
rules: Each generator receives only mutated RCL/Android candidates, semantic intent and deterministic failure diagnostics.
Canonical files, mutation implementation and oracle edits are absent from the generator workspace.
Each trial uses a fresh ephemeral read-only session that cannot edit the authoritative repository, tests, thresholds or evidence.
The evaluator applies only the exact file/old/new edit returned through the frozen JSON Schema.
Every repair must restore exact canonical bytes, Android manifest lowering, native Activity bindings and host transaction replay.
The separate rooted API 35 emulator receipt supplies install, interaction, lifecycle and performance evidence.
Three unique sessions plus GitHub-hosted saved-candidate replay are required before Android AI_GENERATE may pass.

trials.intent: Repair the Android transaction program so one accepted increment adds exactly one while preserving the generic governed transaction path.
Repair the Android input so displayed value and observed changes bind to the same app.input state.
Repair the Android target lifecycle contract so committed RCL state is restored across Activity recreation.

evidenceBoundary: This proves three bounded independent repairs for the frozen K03 Android transaction UI, combined with its separate API 35 emulator receipt. It does not prove arbitrary Android app generation, physical-device parity, Android framework ownership or K400 completion.
